elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: No aggregate monetary cap appears anywhere in the rendered language. Section 11.5 only excludes indirect/consequential damages ("NEITHER PARTY NOR ANY OF ITS AFFILIATES SHALL BE LIABLE FOR INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY, PUNITIVE OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES"); Sections 11.1/11.2 contain unlimited mutual indemnities. The deterministic gate "cap references 12 months of fees or a fixed floor" is false and the proposal adds no cap sentence.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: No cap formula, no fee basis and no USD 1,000,000 floor exist in the operative text, and none was inserted. The only "maximum aggregate" figures cited are Article 6 milestone payment ceilings, which are payment obligations rather than a liability cap.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Section 11.5: "NEITHER PARTY NOR ANY OF ITS AFFILIATES SHALL BE LIABLE FOR INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY, PUNITIVE OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES, INCLUDING LOSS OF PROFITS OR BUSINESS INTERRUPTION" — expressly bilateral.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No cap exists anywhere, so confidentiality liability is unlimited as a matter of substance; Section 11.5(B) additionally carves "A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS OBLIGATIONS UNDER [ARTICLE 9 OR SECTION 5.8]" out of even the consequential-damages exclusion. The condition (a cap that would need a carve-out) does not apply.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: With no aggregate cap in the Agreement, any such liability is unlimited; Section 11.5(B) also references Section 5.8 alongside Article 9. Condition does not apply because there is no cap to carve out of.

Sections 11.1 and 11.2 impose mutual indemnities for "any and all Losses" with no monetary limit, and Section 11.5(D) preserves third-party damages payable under an Article 11 indemnity. No cap constrains them.
No cap exists; Section 11.5 opens "EXCEPT (A) FOR FRAUD, WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR GROSS NEGLIGENCE", so even the damages exclusion does not apply.
Same carve-out: "EXCEPT (A) FOR FRAUD, WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR GROSS NEGLIGENCE"; no aggregate cap exists to limit such liability.
Section 11.5(A) expressly excepts "FRAUD" from the damages exclusion, and no aggregate cap applies to fraud liability.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: There is no cap in the Agreement, so IP-infringement liability is unlimited for both Parties; the absence of an express carve-out is immaterial because the condition (an existing cap) does not apply. Note only that direct IP-infringement claims would still face the Section 11.5 indirect-damages exclusion, which is mutual.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: no cap exists, so AbbVie's Article 6 upfront/milestone/royalty payment obligations are not swept into any cap and Harpoon's recovery of them is unimpaired. Nothing in the rendered text characterises payment obligations as capped damages.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Identical defect at fallback: no aggregate liability cap is created for either Party, and the proposal inserts none. To repair, an operative sentence would have to state that each Party's total aggregate liability shall not exceed a stated amount.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: No cap and no fee-based measure exist. The finding correctly observes the consideration is an upfront/option payment, Article 6 milestones and Net Sales royalties, but that explains rather than satisfies the element; a defined basis (e.g. amounts paid or payable by AbbVie in the preceding 12 months) would need to be drafted.
Mutual "any and all Losses" indemnities in Sections 11.1/11.2 with no monetary limit; Section 11.5(D) preserves indemnified third-party damages.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 11.5(B): "FOR A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS OBLIGATIONS UNDER [ARTICLE 9 OR SECTION 5.8]", and no aggregate cap exists.
Section 11.5(A): "EXCEPT (A) FOR FRAUD, WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR GROSS NEGLIGENCE"; no cap applies.
Section 11.5(A) same carve-out; no cap applies.

reasons: Neither level is position-complete: the two cap elements (mutuality of an aggregate cap and a 12-months-of-fees basis, plus the USD 1,000,000 floor at preferred) are absent from the operative text and no redline supplies them. To close the fallback a drafter would have to insert an express mutual aggregate-liability sentence with a defined monetary basis.

All carve-out elements are met in substance because no cap exists at all — nothing constrains liability for indemnification, confidentiality, data protection/Section 5.8, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement — and Section 11.5's indirect-damages exclusion is expressly bilateral ("NEITHER PARTY").

Because no edits were made, minimality and intent are trivially preserved: no favourable language was deleted, no term left undefined, and no dangling cross-reference created. (The pre-existing redactions at Section 11.5(C) and the bracketed "[ARTICLE 9 OR SECTION 5.8]" are original drafting, not introduced by this proposal.)

No walk-away trigger is present: the regime is symmetric and mutually uncapped, so Customer/AbbVie is not capped while Vendor/Harpoon is uncapped, there is no sub-6-month Vendor cap, and indemnities are not inside any cap. Under the playbook this benefits our party and should not be redlined; the needs_review posture (escalate the trade-off of capping our own Section 11.1 indemnity exposure versus preserving unlimited recourse against Harpoon under Section 11.2 and Article 10) is the correct disposition.

If the deal team does want an outer limit, the operative repair must (i) add a mutual "each Party's total aggregate liability shall not exceed…" sentence, (ii) fix a workable basis (e.g. the greater of amounts paid or payable by AbbVie in the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and a fixed floor), and (iii) expressly place the Section 11.5 exceptions, IP infringement and AbbVie's Article 6 payment obligations outside that cap — otherwise the new cap would swallow the currently uncapped indemnities.
